description:
Some points of interest are more important than others in Grand Theft Auto 6, and airports are always at the top of a player's list of places to see. While airports often play a critical role in a GTA story, they're also useful for knowing where planes are located on the map. We've already covered how to get a plane and other aircraft in GTA 6, but airports are different.

Whether you're looking to steal a plane or land one so you can keep it hidden in a hangar, GTA 6 has several airports and airfields you need to know about. You can see where they're located in Leonida in the guide below.

author: Chris Compendio
description:
I used to firmly believe that Navi from the original Ocarina of Time ruined video games. It’s a completely exaggerated and unscientific take; tutorialization and annoying characters have always existed in the medium. But every time a modern video game character gives me unsolicited verbal advice, or when the protagonist I’m playing as mutters a puzzle solution to themselves, or passive-aggressively suggests where I should go next--short of breaking the fourth wall and looking at me through the TV screen like I’m an idiot--I think of Navi.

While I doubt that Navi directly inspired this game-design precedent that modern AAA games employ far too often, I do think that The Legend of Zelda’s seminal “annoying sidekick” set a precedent for how games disseminate information to the player. Ocarina of Time rightfully receives credit for its influence on how 3D video games are built and how players navigate through 3D spaces. At
title: After The Ocarina Of Time Remake, I Finally Forgive Navi

author: Alessandro Barbosa
description:
Grand Theft Auto VI is a visual and audial treat, and is easily one of the most technically impressive games on the current generation of consoles. But it isn't without issues, especially if you're trying to experience the sights and sounds of Vice City with all the moody contrast and bright highlights that HDR offers.

That's due to an HDR calibration tool that isn't exactly working in the way that you expect it. Like many other games, GTA VI doesn't use the system-level HDR settings on either the PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S. Instead it features its own calibration tool, which lets you adjust the maximum brightness, black levels, and paper white values that work best on your display. While the tool makes calibration seem straightforward, there's an issue with it that makes it very unreliable.
title: Grand Theft Auto 6’s HDR Is Broken, But These Tweaks Can Fix It

author: Joey Carr
description:
The size of Leonida in Grand Theft Auto 6 gives you free rein to do just about anything that your imagination can dream up. Whether you want to explore the Leonida Keys down to the last grain of sand, head out on a long journey to Mount Kalaga, or follow the main story all the way to Vice City, you have dozens of options at your fingertips. However, most of these options are made much easier with a fast car in GTA 6.

We've already covered the fastest cars in GTA 6, but a majority of those cars are unattainable for most, if not all, of the story. There's one exception to that, though, as you can pick up two free legendary-tier Progen Emerus' in GTA 6 just by visiting some specific locations. description:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has plenty of fun Easter eggs--many of which tie back to earlier games in the series--but you can also find a few nods to other megapopular game franchises hiding within the vast map of Leonida. If you take a detour along the north side of Lummox County, you'll come across an area in the woods that looks like it'd be right at home in a Super Mario Bros. game, and you can even collect two distinct caps for your troubles--which might suggest that the greater Mario multiverse theory is true after all.

description:
No, your eyes are not deceiving you and yes, you can truly time travel in GTA 6. Some of you may know the name Tommy Vercetti from 2002's GTA: Vice City. Some of you may not have been born then, but are still old enough to play GTA 6. That's okay, I'm not bitter at all.

Tommy Vercetti was voiced by Ray Liotta, and he was the iconic protagonist from Vice City. Having GTA 6 revisiting Vice City is enough of a reason for Rockstar to throw in one of the game's hugest Easter eggs--you can literally travel back in time to 2002, and you'll grab Tommy Vercetti's shirt and bike as a reward for doing so.
title: How To Get Tommy Vercetti’s Shirt And Bike In GTA 6

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has raised the bar for open-world games, and Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzyński is feeling it. Online, the developer jokingly commented about GTA 6 setting a new gold standard for the genre, a level of quality that makes him want to pack up his Cyberpunk 2 development bags and call it a day.

"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real," Sarzyński wrote online. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle. Cyberpunk 2 is canceled, Imma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now."
title: Cyberpunk 2 Is Canceled, Director Jokes, After GTA 6 Raises The Bar

description:
Nvidia has announced that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as president and CEO of Nvidia, while he'll also return to the Board of Directors. This is happening just hours after US President Donald Trump said Huang should come back.

"The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia," the technology giant said. "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."

description:
There are many weird and wonderful things around Leonida. First of all, there are the GTA 6 WAiNK curiosities--remnants left behind of odd goings on that you can scan to work towards 100% completion. There are rumors of alien abduction, jet-ski-riding dogs, and unexpected cats in your passenger seat. However, one of the weirdest things to happen during my playthrough so far has been stumbling across the Bigfoot mystery.

It all started when I was innocently (read: looking for drugs) wandering through the swampy areas of Leonida, and I found an effigy. I thought this might be a case of accidentally stumbling across something important, and sure enough, when I visited an ATM a few short days afterwards, I spotted a flyer that caught my attention.
